why: Undo and redo are two stacks: executed commands on one, undone commands on the other. UNDO moves the top of the first to the second, REDO moves it back, and a new EXECUTE clears the redo stack. It teaches 'simulate with undo' as stack moves.
hints: Which command does UNDO remove, and which command does REDO bring back?
UNDO removes the most recent active command; REDO restores the most recently undone one. Both are 'last in, first out', so use two stacks: active and redo.
EXECUTE pushes onto active and clears redo; UNDO pops active onto redo (if any); REDO pops redo onto active (if any). After each step output '|'.join(active).
pitfalls: Executing a new command must empty the redo stack.
UNDO on an empty history and REDO with nothing undone are no-ops, but still produce a snapshot.
